findings.title: Hard-coded shared MQTT credentials can expose the fleet control plane
findings.summary: If the credential is active and its ACL reflects the subscriptions in the agents, an attacker can impersonate the control plane or devices, issue fleet commands, read retained status, disrupt receivers, change configurations, and potentially take persistent control of many stations.

confidence.rationale: Direct source trace and centralized validation/attack-path review.

findings.remediation: Rotate immediately, replace with unique per-device principals, and audit wildcard ACLs.

findings.title: MQTT status payload serial is not bound to the authenticated topic serial
findings.summary: A device restricted by broker ACL to its own topic can impersonate a sibling station, poison its online/version/configuration state, create misleading UI telemetry, and potentially overwrite target configuration when that target is currently marked synced.

confidence.rationale: Direct source trace and centralized validation/attack-path review.

findings.remediation: Bind payload serial to the topic serial before all processing and add a two-device regression test.

findings.title: Any one-station overlap grants whole shared-rover credentials and mutation authority
findings.summary: Cross-station correction-stream access, disclosure of a credential valid for unowned mountpoints, and modification/deletion of a shared account used by another station or coordinator.

confidence.rationale: Direct source trace and centralized validation/attack-path review.

findings.remediation: Require all account targets to be within scope or split credentials per station.

findings.title: Device-controlled sync mismatch text reaches an HTML toast sink
findings.summary: A compromised field device can obtain dashboard-origin script execution when an administrator or coordinator investigates its unsynchronized state, enabling theft of browser bearer credentials and commands against every station in the victim's authorized scope.

confidence.rationale: Direct source trace and centralized validation/attack-path review.

findings.remediation: Render toast text safely and add an inert-marker device mismatch test.

findings.title: Coordinator-created viewer fields execute as HTML in the user table
findings.summary: A coordinator can gain script execution in an administrator's user-management session, steal the admin bearer token, change users and station assignments, and pivot to system-wide device/caster operations.

confidence.rationale: Direct source trace and centralized validation/attack-path review.

findings.remediation: Build rows with textContent/property assignment and test coordinator-created markers.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Agent values become stored script in the admin VPN-intelligence table

confidence.rationale: Direct source trace and centralized validation/attack-path review.

findings.remediation: Encode User-Agent output and test the VPN-intelligence table with inert markup.

findings.title: MQTT commands lack freshness and replay protection before destructive actions

confidence.rationale: Direct source trace and centralized validation/attack-path review.

findings.remediation: Add expiry plus durable command-id deduplication and a harmless retained-command test.

confidence.rationale: Direct source trace and centralized validation/attack-path review.
